plan: This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower reduces win probability without improving price paid. With my value at $26, I should bid exactly $26 to ensure optimal outcomes across all possible competitor bid scenarios.

This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. In this setup, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $18. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated interaction to exploit, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses). There's no benefit to bidding above or below my true value of $21, since my payment depends on others' bids, not mine. I'll bid exactly my value.
